title: PRD-4: Adaptive planning depth
description:
Add scale-adaptive planning depth to Ensemble — lightweight path for simple changes, full path for complex

## Problem
Ensemble has fixed PRD→TRD pipeline for all work. BMAD adapts depth based on work complexity.

## Goals
- Simple changes (bug fixes, small features) use lightweight path with minimal overhead
- Complex initiatives use full PRD→TRD pipeline
- Complexity detection auto-classifies work before planning begins

## User Stories
- As a developer fixing a bug, I want lightweight path so I don't write a PRD for a 1-line fix
- As a lead, I want adaptive depth so team right-sizes planning effort to work complexity

## Requirements
- FR-001: classify command detects work complexity (Simple/Medium/Complex)
- FR-002: Simple work → fix-issue path (no PRD/TRD)
- FR-003: Medium work → create-prd + implement-trd
- FR-004: Complex work → full PRD→TRD→implement pipeline
- FR-005: Complexity classification exposed to user for override

## Verification
- Bug fix classified as Simple → fix-issue path
- New feature classified as Complex → full pipeline

title: Add multi-reviewer share-URL fan-out to refinement-review
description:
## Problem

ensemble-full-refine-prd --collab --tunnel=quick currently mints exactly ONE share URL per session (packages/core/lib/refinement-review/server.js:768-773 in startServer; server.js:839-844 in setTunnelUrl). The /api/exchange handler atomically burns the nonce (server.js:89-99 via consumeNonce), so the second reviewer hitting the same URL gets 401 'invalid or expired nonce' and is locked out.

The mental model that 'each reviewer redeems their own copy of the URL within the TTL' is not actually true: the nonce map is keyed by id, identical URLs share one nonce, and there is no HTTP route to mint additional nonces (full route list: /api/exchange, /api/events, /api/session, /api/document, PATCH /api/questions/:id, POST /api/comments, PATCH /api/comments/:id, /api/complete). mintNonce is exported under _internal (server.js:884) and is callable only in-process.

## Goal

Let the operator fan out N independent share URLs for one session so multiple reviewers can join concurrently.

## Scope (minimum viable)

- Add result.createShareUrl() to the result object returned by startServer (server.js:808-819). Mints a fresh nonce against the current publicUrl and returns { reviewUrl, shareNonce }. In-process only; no HTTP route required.
- Bootstrap CLI flag --reviewers <N> that calls createShareUrl() N times and logs all N URLs.
- Test: confirm N independent reviewer URLs all redeem successfully and each reviewer gets an independent review-sid cookie bound to the same session.
- Update the refinement review guide to document the multi-reviewer flow + the security trade-off (each URL is single-use; leak window = NONCE_TTL_MS = 10 min).

## Out of scope

- N-use nonces (rejected: trades leaked-URL-permanence for first-hit-locks-out, opposite of current threat model).
- Authenticated /api/share route (operator-side fan-out matches the current threat model; per-reviewer invite is a v2 concern).
- Changes to bearer or cookie session semantics.

## Acceptance

- startServer().createShareUrl() returns a fresh { reviewUrl, shareNonce } each call, bound to the same opts.sessionPath.
- Calling createShareUrl() N times yields N independent URLs.
- Following URL[k] sets a review-sid cookie distinct from URL[j] for k != j, both authenticated to the same session.
- Bootstrap with --reviewers 3 logs 3 URLs and the SPA loads for each.

## Notes

- Discovered during PRD-2026-019 refinement session 2026-08-12.
- The current single-reviewer flow is preserved; this is additive.
- Nonce TTL is 10 min (NONCE_TTL_MS at server.js).
close_reason: Implementation complete: createShareUrl() on result object; --reviewers N (1-50) parameter; bootstrap restructure tunnel→reviewers→await→read→recap; N=1 output preserved; 46/46 server tests passing; YAML/SKILL/prompt/guide regenerated. Committed ca1d638 on feature/refinement-review-tunnel.

title: PRD-5: Scale-adaptive intelligence
description:
Implement AI-driven complexity analysis that auto-adjusts Ensemble planning depth

## Problem
Ensemble requires manual complexity classification. BMAD uses scale-adaptive intelligence to auto-adjust.

## Goals
- AI analyzes work description to determine complexity
- Planning depth auto-selected based on complexity score
- Complexity score based on: scope size, dependencies, risk factors, team size

## User Stories
- As a developer, I want auto-selected planning depth so I don't manually classify work
- As a PM, I want AI complexity scoring so planning effort matches actual need

## Requirements
- FR-001: analyze-complexity command scores work description
- FR-002: Score 1-3 → Simple (fix-issue path)
- FR-003: Score 4-6 → Medium (PRD→TRD)
- FR-004: Score 7-10 → Complex (full pipeline with extra review)
- FR-005: Complexity score shown to user before planning begins
- FR-006: User can override AI classification

## Verification
- Simple bug description → score ≤3 → fix-issue path
- Complex initiative description → score ≥7 → full pipeline with extra gates

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
# br-ivv Adversarial Phrase False-Positive Log — ensemble-as-behaviors @ 71ca738+

Run 2026-09-23. 12 prompt-templates x 43 registry phrases = **516 probes** through the
real hook (`node packages/router/hooks/router.js`, stdin JSON), block-parsed for
`→ skill <name>` lines. Scripts: `scripts/adversarial-phrase-sweep.js` (raw rows →
`/tmp/ivv-raw.json`), `scripts/adversarial-phrase-report.js` (precision tables).
Reproducible: `node scripts/adversarial-phrase-sweep.js && node scripts/adversarial-phrase-report.js`.

## Result headline

- **0 unexpected skill activations.** Every firing on every probe is an exact substring
  hit on some phrase, by the documented matching contract.
- **473/473 negative-intent probes fired ≥1 skill** — 100% "false positive" by intent,
  but **462/473 are own-phrase hits** (the negation/question/trap template still contains
  the literal phrase → the owning skill surfaces). That is substring matching working
  exactly as designed; suggestion-only + "act only if it fits" framing absorbs the cost.
- **516/516 positive probes fired correctly**, 12/12 templates per phrase (perfect recall).
- **12 cross-phrase hits, one cause** — the entire precision loss of the registry in one row:

## Ambiguous phrases

| skill | phrase | defect | impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git-town` | `create a pr` | prefix of `create a prd` / `create a trd` (all prompts mentioning those phrases also surface git-town) | the ONLY collision: 12/516 probes |

**Recommendation for REQ-BEH-002**: add word-boundary to `create a pr`
(`" … \bcreate a pr\b"`-style — longest-match-wins, or exclude when followed by `d`/`ov`/`o`)
or drop the phrase — git-town is already covered by `create a pull request`.

## Per-phrase precision (all 43: identical shape)

Every phrase: `neg firings 11/11` (own-phrase substring, by design), `pos firings 1/1`,
`extra-skill hits` 0 except the 10 `create a pr*`-family rows. Full table:
`/tmp/ivv-report.md` (session-local; regenerate with the report script).

## False-negative companion note (from br-fnf run)

Prompts that name the artifact WITHOUT a registered verb-phrase — e.g.
"I need a PRD for the billing feature", "we should write requirements for X" — match
**zero** phrases (substring contract has no noun-only patterns). Recall gaps are in verb
phrasing coverage, not false positives. Candidates to seed: `draft the requirements`,
`spec out` (present), `requirements doc` (noun form), `PRD for`, `TRD for`.
Feeds REQ-BEH-002 alongside the collision fix.

## Method limits

- Templates cover 11 negative forms (negation x3, already-done, substring-trap, quoted-meta,
  what/why questions, past-tense, compound-neg, embedded-word) + 1 positive; no typos, no
  non-English, no multi-intent prompts.
- Registry as of 71ca738: 43 phrases / 6 skills. `glob` is a root devDependency; the sweep
  runs from the repo root.

title: PRD-1: Hard-enforce constitution
description:
Implement hard-gate constitution enforcement in Ensemble spec/plan phases

## Problem
Ensemble currently uses soft-gate enforcement — constitution violations pause and allow override. Spec-Kit's Nine Articles are enforced as blocking phase gates.

## Goals
- Constitution violations during create-prd/create-trd BLOCK generation, no override option
- Constitutional compliance verified before phase completion
- Violations produce actionable error messages referencing specific constitution articles

## User Stories
- As a developer, I want hard-gate enforcement so my team cannot bypass architecture standards
- As a PM, I want constitution as blocking gate so spec reviews catch violations early

## Requirements
- FR-001: create-prd phase blocks if constitution violated; no skip/override flag
- FR-002: create-trd phase blocks if constitution violated; no skip/override flag
- FR-003: Violation error messages reference constitution article number
- FR-004: Soft-gate mode removed from constitution enforcement code

## Verification
- Test with violating PRD: expect hard block, not pause
- Test with violating TRD: expect hard block, not pause

comments.text:
# br-rmw Multi-Skill Collision Ordering Audit — ensemble-as-behaviors

Run 2026-09-23. Script: `scripts/collision-order-audit.js` (reproducible:
`node scripts/collision-order-audit.js`; exits non-zero on any nondeterminism, sort
violation, or unexpected hit set).

## Contract under audit

`matchPhrases` output must be: deduped by `skill|phrase`, sorted by skill name, then
phrase-alphabetical within a skill (longest-phrase-first is NOT the contract —
`localeCompare` on phrase is). `buildPhraseBlock` renders in that array order.

## Method

- 8 hand-built compound probes (multi-skill prompts: PRD+git-town, TRD+pull-request,
  three merging-a-pr phrases in one prompt, etc.)
- 30 exhaustive pair probes: first phrase of every skill pair, both orderings.
- Each probe run 5x through the REAL hook (`execFileSync` + stdin JSON); outputs
  compared for byte-identity AND against the independently-computed expected hit set
  (substring test against the full registry).

## Results

- **Determinism: 38/38 probes × 5 runs byte-identical.** No ordering jitter.
- **Sort contract: PASS on every probe** — skill-major, phrase-alpha within skill, e.g.
  `creating-a-prd/create a prd` → `git-town/create a feature branch` →
  `git-town/create a pr`.
- **3/8 compound probes surface multi-skill collisions** (`create a prd` ∋
  `create a pr`, `create a trd` ∋ …): identical root cause as the `br-ivv` finding —
  git-town's `create a pr` phrase is a strict prefix of `create a prd`/`create a trd`.
  Ordering itself stays deterministic; the collision is a registry-content issue, not a
  comparator bug. Fix belongs with br-ivv's recommendation (word-boundary or drop).
- All 30 pair probes: skill order strictly alphabetical regardless of phrase order in
  the prompt.

## Verdict

Ordering is correct and deterministic; the audit script is a permanent regression guard
(exit≠0 on drift). Recorded: collisions observed == predicted from the prefix overlap;
no additional ambiguous pairs beyond `br-ivv`'s table.

title: Long-lived review session with auto-port, QuickTunnel, 6h TTL, username gate, presence
description:
## Goal

Add a `--long-lived` mode to the refinement-review server that:
- Picks a port automatically (OS-assigned).
- Implicitly tunnels via Cloudflare QuickTunnel to expose the public URL.
- Self-terminates after a TTL (default 6h) or on completion, whichever first.
- Requires a username before serving the document.
- Shows a live presence list of who is currently viewing.

## Invocation

```
/ensemble:refine-prd --collab --long-lived docs/PRD/PRD-2026-019.md
/ensemble:refine-trd --collab --long-lived docs/TRD/TRD-2026-019-*.md
```

## Behavior

- Server picks port (OS-assigned, ephemeral within the process lifetime).
- QuickTunnel auto-tunnels to a public URL on `*.trycloudflare.com`; same flow as today's `--tunnel=quick` but implicit in `--long-lived`.
- Bootstrap prints `Invite URL: https://<random>.trycloudflare.com/api/exchange?invite=<token>` once. Operator shares via Slack/Teams manually.
- TTL timer: server self-terminates after `--ttl` (default 6h) or on Complete, whichever first. Cleanup tears down QuickTunnel and closes the listener.
- Exchange page: GET /api/exchange?invite=<id> validates the invite against an in-memory multi-use map (no burn), returns a username form with `invite` as a hidden field. POST /api/identify { name, invite } re-validates the invite (same map, no burn), validates `name` (non-empty, length-bounded), mints a `review-sid` cookie bound to `displayName`, redirects to document. POST with missing/invalid invite returns 401 and mints no cookie.
- Presence: in-memory `Map<sid, { name, connectedAt, count }>`; a single sid may own multiple concurrent EventSource connections (multiple tabs per reviewer). Increment on connect, decrement on close; delete the entry and broadcast `event: viewers` only when the count reaches 0. Broadcast fires only on 0↔1 transitions (no event churn on intra-sid tab churn). UI renders "Currently viewing" row deduped by sid. No persistence to `session.json`. Existing server-side keepalive comments (`: heartbeat\n\n`, 25s) remain for proxy survival and are ignored by EventSource for presence purposes.

## Acceptance

1. `--long-lived` (no `--ttl`) → server exits at 6h.
2. `--long-lived --ttl=24h` → server exits at 24h.
3. `--long-lived --ttl=7d` → server exits at 7d.
4. `--long-lived --ttl=1h` → bootstrap aborts with `--ttl must be at least 6h`.
5. Username gate: GET /api/exchange?invite=<valid> returns the form (200, HTML); POST /api/identify { name, invite } with valid invite mints the cookie and redirects to the document; the document is only served after identification (no sid cookie → 401).
6. Presence: two browsers with different names see each other on the "viewers" row within 2s.
7. Presence cleanup: when the LAST SSE request for a given sid closes (count → 0), that viewer is removed from the presence map and the updated list is broadcast synchronously. Closing any non-final tab (count > 0) does NOT remove the viewer. Unit-tested by explicitly closing the request/socket (no browser).
8. Presence is in-memory: server crash → no stale entries anywhere; restart is uneventful.
9. Mode exclusivity: `--long-lived` and `--reviewers N` mutually exclusive (clean error). `--long-lived` and `--tunnel=quick` are compatible (QuickTunnel is implicit in `--long-lived`).
10. Multi-tab: a sid with two concurrent SSE connections; closing one does NOT remove the viewer from the broadcast; closing the second does.
11. Invite enforcement: POST /api/identify with missing invite → 401, no cookie minted, no redirect. POST /api/identify with invalid invite → 401, no cookie minted, no redirect. The same valid invite may be used by multiple reviewers (multi-use; no burn on POST success).

## Defaults

- `--ttl`: optional positive duration; 6h default. Format follows existing project duration parser. Must be >= 6h (extension-only).
- QuickTunnel: implicit when `--long-lived`; no separate flag.
- Username: free-text, no uniqueness check, no auth.
- Presence: `Map<sid, { name, connectedAt, count }>` refcounted by sid; multi-tab reviewers stay visible until their last tab closes. Broadcast only on 0↔1 transitions (synchronous removal + `event: viewers` broadcast on count→0).
- Cookie schema gains `displayName`; no other auth changes.

## Out of scope

- Manual invite revocation API.
- Manual token rotation.
- Auto-share webhook integration (Slack/Teams incoming webhook).
- Presence persistence across restart.
- Named tunnel / external stable origin support (in-process QuickTunnel only).
- TTL cap/warning policy.

## Sibling

- br-68h: multi-reviewer share-URL fan-out via transient nonces (same-day).
- This bead: long-lived review session via QuickTunnel + in-memory invite + 6h TTL (across days within a single process lifetime).

title: PRD-3: quickstart.md validation artifact
description:
Generate quickstart.md from acceptance criteria for QA manual smoke test runbook

## Problem
Ensemble produces specs but no derived validation runbook for QA.

## Goals
- Generate quickstart.md from TRD acceptance criteria
- Provides manual smoke test scenarios for QA team
- Scenarios derived directly from ACs, ensuring coverage

## User Stories
- As QA lead, I want quickstart.md so I have manual test scenarios covering all ACs
- As PM, I want validated acceptance criteria that produce testable scenarios

## Requirements
- FR-001: implement-trd generates quickstart.md from ACs
- FR-002: Each AC maps to ≥1 test scenario
- FR-003: Scenarios include setup steps, actions, expected results
- FR-004: Format suitable for manual test execution (checkboxes)

## Verification
- quickstart.md exists after implement-trd completion
- Each AC has corresponding test scenario
